item.title: Election of 1828 and the right to vote, by state (data for lessons) v1.1
item.snippet: Electoral votes for Andrew Jackson and John Quincy Adams in 1828, how each state chose its electors, and who could vote there, for the 24 states of 1828.
item.description:
One polygon for each of the 24 states in the election of 1828, made for US History map lessons. Electoral votes are from the National Archives (archives.gov/electoral-college/1828). How each state chose its presidential electors, and who could vote there (property and tax rules for white men, and whether free Black men could vote), were researched from state constitutions and laws and checked independently; each state's main source is in RulesSource and RulesSourceURL.

Women could not vote in any state in 1828 (New Jersey ended women's voting in 1807). Today's state outlines from Natural Earth, with West Virginia shown as part of Virginia; territories are not shown.
item.credits: Electoral votes: National Archives. Voting rules: state constitutions and laws as cited in each record. Outlines: Natural Earth (public domain).
